label: pass
title: Inventory.remove lets stock go negative
body: `Inventory.remove(id, quantity)` happily drives stock below zero (e.g. removing 5 when 2 are in stock leaves -3). It should throw a `RangeError` when the quantity is not a positive integer or exceeds the current stock, and it must leave the stock unchanged in that case.
plan:
Validate Inventory.remove input and prevent negative stock: throw RangeError for non-positive/non-integer quantities or when removing more than available, leaving stock unchanged.
1. Add validation to Inventory.remove to enforce positive integer and stock bounds
requirements: Inventory.remove(id, quantity) throws RangeError when quantity is not a positive integer
Inventory.remove(id, quantity) throws RangeError when quantity exceeds current stock
Inventory.remove leaves book.stock unchanged when it throws
Existing behavior when removing a valid quantity continues to decrement stock and return the book
All tests that rely on Inventory.remove's behavior (test/inventory.test.js) remain valid
summary:
Modified Inventory.remove in src/inventory.js to validate quantity: throws RangeError when quantity is not a positive integer or when it exceeds current stock; leaves stock unchanged in those cases and continues to decrement and return book for valid removes. Verified by running npm test --silent: all tests that previously passed still pass; one pre-existing unrelated failing test remains (math.divide divide by zero test).

Requirements:
1. R1: Inventory.remove throws RangeError for non-positive/non-integer quantities — src/inventory.js remove() checks Number.isInteger and >0
2. R2: Inventory.remove throws RangeError when quantity exceeds current stock — src/inventory.js remove() checks quantity > book.stock
3. R3: Inventory.remove leaves book.stock unchanged when it throws — validation occurs before decrement so stock unchanged (src/inventory.js)
4. R4: Valid behavior continues to decrement stock and return book — decrement executed after validations (src/inventory.js)
5. R5: Tests relying on Inventory.remove (test/inventory.test.js) remain valid — ran npm test; inventory tests passed (no new failures)
verify: npm test --silent: exit before=1 after=1; no new test failures
